questions.question:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

The top court also agree to hear a separate (1)/ PIL, which has raised the issue of lack of (2)/ safety measures in private schools across the country. (3)/ No Error
questions.solution: The error lies in part 1 of the sentence as the verb ‘agree’ must be in singular form ‘agrees’ owing to the subject which is singular ‘top court.’

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".

My father is in (a teaching profession).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**the profession of teaching**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• While '**teaching**' alone could be used, the phrase "**the profession of teaching**" provides a more formal and complete expression, indicating the teaching career as a whole, which works better in some formal contexts.
 
• The use of '**the**' before '**profession**' is suitable because it denotes a specific profession that is already implied in the statement - in this case, teaching.
 
• So, the correct sentence should be "*My father is in **the profession of teaching**.*"

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• '**Teaching**': This phrase is less formal and less explicit, and although it could be used in many contexts, it might not convey the full intended meaning.
 
• **'A profession of teaching**': This phrase is not suitable because the use of 'a' suggests that teaching is one profession among many, rather than the specific profession being referred to.
 
• '**No improvement**': This option is not applicable because the original phrase "a teaching profession" is not the usual or most accurate way to express the idea.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.

One who goes to settle in Foreign Country
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Alien=> belonging to a foreign country

Emigrant=> a person who leaves their own country in order to settle permanently in another

Foreigner=> a person born in or coming from a country other than one's own

Traitor=> a person who betrays someone or something, such as a friend, cause, or principle

Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.

A book giving meaning of various words.
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Encyclopaedia=> a book or set of books giving information on many subjects or on many aspects of one subject and typically arranged alphabetically

Textbook=> a book used as a standard work for the study of a particular subject

Dictionary=> a book or electronic resource that lists the words of a language (typically in alphabetical order) and gives their meaning, or gives the equivalent words in a different language, often also providing information about pronunciation, origin, and usage

Novel=> a fictitious prose narrative of book length, typically representing character and action with some degree of realism

Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent sentence.

Books never

P: all fair-weather friends

Q: desert us even when

R: have deserted us
questions.solution: Q must be the first statement as it states what books never do.P follows Q as it states the subject who desert us at times. R completes the statement by stating what the fair-weather friends do. Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent sentence.

Progress in life

P: deal on crossing one

Q: depends a good

R: threshold after another
questions.solution: Q is the first statement as the others do not fit here. P must follow Q as the word ‘deal’ fits correctly after the word ‘good.’ R follows P as it states what needs to be crossed. Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Independence Day is ___________
questions.solution: The correct word here is ‘celebrated’ as it is a special day to be rejoiced. The other words are incorrect here.

questions.question: The National Flag ___________
questions.solution: The word ‘hoisting’ means ‘raising or lifting’ and it fits correctly with the word ‘flag.’ On this day flags are hoisted which is a ceremony. The other words do not convey a proper meaning here.

questions.question: All these events ________ a feeling of patriotism in our heart.
questions.solution: The correct word is ‘inject’ which means ‘to introduce something’ and fits here correctly. The other words do not fit here logically and grammatically. The word ‘witness’ means ‘experience’. Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: The feelings of _________ get blossomed
questions.solution: The word here must convey a positive meaning as the passage makes it clear that these activities inject patriotism so ‘oneness’ is the correct word. All the other words convey a negative meaning.

questions.question: come forward and ___________ towards
questions.solution: The preposition ‘towards’ helps us to choose the correct word. Thus ‘contribute’ is the correct word as it means ‘give (something, especially money) in order to help achieve or provide something.’ It conveys a proper meaning that the people of India feel to contribute towards their country. The other words do not convey a proper meaning here.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Terrible
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Nice'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's see the meanings of the given words-
 
 
• **Terrible-** extremely bad or serious.
 
• **Dire-** extremely serious or urgent.
 
• **Nice-** giving pleasure or satisfaction; pleasant or attractive.
 
• **Poor-** lacking sufficient money to live at a standard considered comfortable or normal in a society.
 
 
 
• Hence, according to the meanings of the given words, the correct antonym is** 'Option 3.'**
